sources.entry: RAG Citation Coverage Auditor - Offline CLI that checks declared RAG answer citations against approved retrieval sources and explicit claim support in local exports. #free #opensource #rag

summary.one_liner: An offline, read-only Node.js CLI that audits a local JSON export of RAG answer claims and citation IDs against approved retrieval sources and explicit source-to-claim support.
summary.what_it_does: It reads a named local JSON export containing sources (with approval, permissions, observation date and supported-claim lists) and claims (with citation IDs). It checks whether each citation ID resolves to a declared source, whether that source is approved, permitted for a requested scope and fresh relative to an operator-supplied date, and whether at least one usable source explicitly lists the claim as supported. It reports three metrics (resolved citations, usable citations, covered claims) as numerator/denominator pairs, with null where evidence is unknown. Output is a JSON report on stdout with findings sorted by location and rule ID, and a short human summary on stderr when --json is absent. It does not fetch sources, judge claim truth, or extract citations from Markdown.
use_cases: audit citations in a RAG answer export
check that cited sources are approved and in scope
detect fabricated or unresolved citation IDs
verify claims have explicitly supporting sources
flag stale retrieval sources before publishing answers
run citation coverage checks in CI
notable: Treats a cited ID as not proof of support; requires an explicit source-to-claim support relation in the export
Reports unknown approval, permission, freshness or inventory as incomplete rather than passing them
Zero runtime and development dependencies; writes no files and contacts no network or provider
Configurable bounds on bytes, sources, claims, citations, depth and time, with deterministic byte-identical reports
Frozen rule table with fixed severities and exit codes (0 pass, 1 fail, 2 incomplete or invalid)
caveats: Audits only a local export; it does not verify that support relations are true or retrieve sources
Requires the operator to supply --as-of; the tool never reads the calendar date
Time limit checks are cooperative, so elapsed time can exceed the configured timeout slightly
keywords: make sure answers cite approved sources
